disclaimer: Reference fixture in the simulator trace schema (v3). The scenarios are written by hand, but every function, theorem, predicate, right, syscall number and error they name is the kernel's own: the sync resolves each declaration in the pinned seLe4n checkout and fails if one is missing. The validator re-runs every capability lookup, rights check, flow check and scheduling decision against the state and refuses a trace that disagrees. The kernel does not yet export JSON traces; when it does (source == "kernel"), steps become a replay of a real run.

propertyCatalog.label: No capability, no access
propertyCatalog.statement: A syscall reaches its operation only after the caller's CSpace resolves the named slot to a capability carrying the right that syscall requires; the lookup itself changes no state.

propertyCatalog.label: Derived authority never grows
propertyCatalog.statement: A minted capability names the same object as its parent and carries a subset of the parent's rights.

propertyCatalog.label: A refused syscall changes nothing
propertyCatalog.statement: A kernel transition has type SystemState → Except KernelError (α × SystemState): an error carries no successor state, so every refusal leaves the system exactly as it was.
propertyCatalog.caveat: This holds by the type of a transition rather than by a separate theorem.

propertyCatalog.label: Non-interference
propertyCatalog.statement: Every NonInterferenceStep, and every trace of them, preserves low-equivalence: what an observer at one security level can see does not depend on higher-level state.
propertyCatalog.caveat: Stated over the NonInterferenceStep relation (35 constructors). The theorem over the live checked syscall entry holds given a per-arm hypothesis.

propertyCatalog.label: IPC never flows down the lattice
propertyCatalog.statement: The endpoint flow gate admits a message only if the global security lattice allows the flow from sender to receiver; an endpoint override can narrow that, never widen it.

propertyCatalog.label: Memory isolation
propertyCatalog.statement: Carving from untyped memory preserves the untyped-memory invariant: watermarks stay inside their regions and carved children never overlap. Distinct address-space roots carry distinct ASIDs.

propertyCatalog.label: W^X: no page is writable and executable
propertyCatalog.statement: Any successful mapping was given W^X-compliant permissions: the argument decoder (PagePermissions.ofNat?) refuses a writable and executable permission word, so no page table entry is ever written with both.

propertyCatalog.label: Invariant preservation
propertyCatalog.statement: The syscall entry preserves proofLayerInvariantBundle, the 16-conjunct composition of every subsystem invariant.
propertyCatalog.caveat: Compositional: the theorem takes, as a hypothesis, that the dispatched operation preserves the bundle, and per-operation preservation theorems discharge it arm by arm.

propertyCatalog.label: Scheduling discipline
propertyCatalog.statement: The per-core selector picks the best thread of the highest-priority bucket (priority, then earliest deadline, then FIFO), and a scheduling context can never consume more than 8 × its budget.
propertyCatalog.caveat: Optimality is stated over the maximum-priority bucket, not the whole queue; the CBS bound is the static 8 × budget ceiling. There is no unconditional no-starvation theorem.

invariantCatalog.label: Endpoint queues well-formed
invariantCatalog.meaning: Every endpoint's send and receive queues are well-formed intrusive lists whose members are blocked on that endpoint.

invariantCatalog.label: No thread queued twice
invariantCatalog.meaning: No thread appears twice in an endpoint queue.

invariantCatalog.label: Blocked threads are not runnable
invariantCatalog.meaning: A thread blocked on send, receive, reply or a notification is never in a run queue.

invariantCatalog.label: Notification waiters consistent
invariantCatalog.meaning: A notification's waiter list holds exactly the threads blocked on it.

invariantCatalog.label: Reply waiters consistent
invariantCatalog.meaning: A thread blocked on a reply waits on another live thread, and a reply object names its caller only while that caller is blocked on the reply.

invariantCatalog.label: Running thread is not queued
invariantCatalog.meaning: The thread a core is running is not also in its run queue.

invariantCatalog.label: Current thread is a TCB
invariantCatalog.meaning: Whatever a core records as its current thread is a thread control block in the object store.

invariantCatalog.label: Budget within bounds
invariantCatalog.meaning: A scheduling context's remaining budget never exceeds its configured budget.

invariantCatalog.label: Derivation links agree
invariantCatalog.meaning: Every derivation link joins two occupied slots, and each slot has at most one parent: the tree the kernel walks to revoke is the tree the slots describe.

invariantCatalog.label: Derivation tree acyclic
invariantCatalog.meaning: No capability is derived, directly or transitively, from itself.

invariantCatalog.label: Untyped watermark in bounds
invariantCatalog.meaning: Each untyped's allocation watermark stays inside its region.

invariantCatalog.label: Carved objects never overlap
invariantCatalog.meaning: The children carved from one untyped occupy disjoint memory.

invariantCatalog.label: No writable+executable page
invariantCatalog.meaning: No mapping in any address space is both writable and executable.

invariantCatalog.label: ASIDs unique
invariantCatalog.meaning: Each ASID names at most one address-space root.

invariantCatalog.label: No stale TLB entries
invariantCatalog.meaning: Every cached translation corresponds to a live mapping; an unmap shoots the entry down.

invariantCatalog.label: Audit log bounded
invariantCatalog.meaning: The declassification audit log never exceeds its capacity; a full log refuses the downgrade.

scenarios.title: Call and reply through an endpoint
scenarios.summary: A server waits on an endpoint with a reply object; a client calls it, the server answers through the reply object, and the client resumes with the answer. Every hop is a queue operation on the kernel's own objects.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The server (priority 120) runs on core 0 and the client (priority 100) waits in the run queue. The server holds the endpoint with read, write and grant, and a reply object; the client holds the same endpoint with write only, minted with badge 17, so the server can tell which client is calling.

steps.title: server: receive on the endpoint

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the endpoint)
Require the read right
Endpoint → receiver flow gate
Receive; no sender waits, so block with the reply object stashed

steps.narrative: x0 = 1 walks the server's CSpace to slot 1, the endpoint capability, which carries the read right a receive needs. The flow gate admits endpoint → server. Because msgInfo.length is 1, x2 names a reply object: slot 2 resolves to it. No sender is queued, so the server joins the endpoint's receive queue, stashes the reply object for the next caller, and leaves the core.

steps.title: core 0: pick the next thread
steps.narrative: The server left the core, so on the way out of the kernel the scheduler picks again. The client is the only runnable thread, so it is dispatched and leaves the run queue (a running thread is never queued).

steps.title: client: call the service

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the badged endpoint)
Require the write right
Caller → endpoint flow gate
Rendezvous with the waiting server, then block on the reply

steps.narrative: The client's slot 1 holds the endpoint with write, which a call needs. The flow gate admits client → endpoint. The server is waiting, so the kernel pops it off the receive queue and hands it the two message words, the label and the capability's badge, 17. The server becomes runnable on its home core. The client blocks on the reply, and the server's stashed reply object now names the client as its caller.

steps.title: core 0: pick the next thread
steps.narrative: The client blocked, so core 0 picks again: the server is the only runnable thread.

steps.title: server: reply

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 2, the reply object)
Require the write right
Transfer the reply to the caller the reply object names

steps.narrative: The reply resolves through the reply object, not through the endpoint: slot 2 names rp.svc, and rp.svc names the client. The kernel checks server → client against the flow policy (a refusal here would be replyCapInvalid, not flowDenied), delivers the reply word, unlinks the caller from the reply object and wakes the client. The server keeps the core: the client's priority is lower, so nothing preempts it.

steps.title: server: receive again

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the endpoint)
Require the read right
Endpoint → receiver flow gate
Receive; no sender waits, so block

steps.narrative: The server goes back to waiting for the next call, with the same reply object, which is free again.

steps.title: core 0: the client resumes
steps.narrative: The client is dispatched and returns from its call with the server's answer, 49, in its first message register.

scenarios.title: The capability gate
scenarios.summary: Four syscalls from a thread holding one read-only endpoint capability. Three are refused, at the stage that refuses them and with the error it returns; each refusal leaves the state exactly as it was.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The app thread's CSpace is a 16-slot CNode with a 4-bit guard of 0, so a CPtr's low 8 bits are its address: the top 4 must match the guard and the bottom 4 pick the slot. Slot 1 holds an endpoint capability with the read right only.

steps.title: app: send with a read-only capability

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1)
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send

steps.narrative: x0 = 1 resolves: guard 0 matches and slot 1 holds the endpoint. But a send needs write and the capability carries only read, so the lookup refuses with illegalAuthority. Nothing after the gate runs and nothing changes.

steps.title: app: call through an empty slot

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 5)
Require the write right
Caller → endpoint flow gate
Call

steps.narrative: x0 = 5: the guard matches, but slot 5 is empty. There is no capability to check rights against, so the lookup refuses with invalidCapability.

steps.title: app: send through a guard mismatch

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (guard 3, slot 1)
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send

steps.narrative: x0 = 0x31: the low 4 bits select slot 1, which is occupied, but the 4 bits above them read 3 and the CNode's guard is 0. A CPtr whose guard does not match resolves to nothing, so the lookup refuses before it ever reads the slot.

steps.title: app: receive, which the capability allows

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1)
Require the read right
Endpoint → receiver flow gate
Receive; nothing is queued, so block

steps.narrative: The same capability does carry read, which is what a receive needs. msgInfo.length is 0, so the receive names no reply object. Nothing is queued on the endpoint, so the app blocks on it and leaves the core.

steps.title: core 0: nothing to run
steps.narrative: No thread is runnable, so core 0 runs nothing until an interrupt or another core wakes something.

scenarios.title: Notifications: signals and badges
scenarios.summary: A driver signals a handler three times. The first signal wakes the waiting handler; the next two find nobody waiting and accumulate as a bitwise OR in the notification word, which the handler collects in one wait.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The handler is blocked on the alarm notification. The driver runs; both have priority 80. The driver's capability can signal (write), the handler's can wait (read).

steps.title: driver: signal badge 0b001

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the notification)
Require the write right
Signaller → notification flow gate
Signal

steps.narrative: The handler is waiting, so the badge does not touch the notification word: the kernel pops the handler off the wait queue and delivers badge 1 straight to it, after checking that the flow onward to the handler is allowed too. The handler becomes runnable but does not preempt the driver: equal priority never does.

steps.title: driver: signal badge 0b100

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the notification)
Require the write right
Signaller → notification flow gate
Signal

steps.narrative: Nobody waits now, so the badge is stored: the notification becomes active with word 0b100.

steps.title: driver: signal badge 0b010

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the notification)
Require the write right
Signaller → notification flow gate
Signal

steps.narrative: A second signal with nobody waiting ORs into the word: 0b100 | 0b010 = 0b110. Signals coalesce; the word records which sources fired, not how often.

steps.title: driver: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Charge the rest of the slice, requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: Yield names no capability, so the path goes straight from decode to the scheduler. The driver's time slice is reset and it goes to the tail of its priority bucket, behind the handler, which the scheduler then picks.

steps.title: handler: wait, collecting 0b110

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the notification)
Require the read right
Notification → waiter flow gate
Wait; the word is set, so take it without blocking

steps.narrative: The notification is active, so the wait returns at once with the accumulated word, 0b110, and clears it. The handler learns that sources 1 and 2 both fired.

steps.title: handler: wait again

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the notification)
Require the read right
Notification → waiter flow gate
Wait; the word is clear, so block

steps.narrative: Nothing is pending, so the handler joins the wait queue and leaves the core.

steps.title: core 0: the driver resumes
steps.narrative: The handler blocked, so the driver, the only runnable thread, is dispatched.

scenarios.title: Priority buckets and round robin
scenarios.summary: Three threads share priority 50 and one sits at 10. Timer ticks spend the running thread's slice; when it runs out the thread goes to the tail of its bucket and the head of the highest bucket runs. The priority-10 thread never runs while a priority-50 thread can.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: Thread a runs with 2 ticks left of its slice. b and c wait in the priority-50 bucket, d in the priority-10 bucket. The run queue keeps insertion order within each bucket.

steps.title: tick: a has 1 tick left
steps.narrative: A timer tick charges the running thread one tick of its slice. a has 1 left and keeps the core.

steps.title: tick: a's slice runs out
steps.narrative: The tick finds a on its last tick. Its slice is refilled to 5 and it goes to the tail of the priority-50 bucket, behind b and c. The scheduler scans the highest bucket in order and takes its head, b. d is not considered: the bucket above it has runnable threads.

steps.title: b: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Charge the rest of the slice, requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: b gives up the rest of its slice. It is requeued at the tail of its bucket, and the bucket's new head, c, runs.

steps.title: tick: c spends a tick
steps.narrative: c has a fresh slice and spends one tick of it. The bucket now reads a, b behind c; d is still waiting below.

scenarios.title: Budgets and earliest deadline first
scenarios.summary: Three threads at one priority, each bound to a scheduling context. A thread whose budget runs out is ineligible until it is replenished; among the eligible, the earliest deadline wins.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: alpha runs with 1 tick of budget left. beta (deadline 25) and gamma (deadline 18) wait at the same priority. Deadlines and budgets live in each thread's scheduling context.

steps.title: tick: alpha's budget runs out
steps.narrative: The tick spends alpha's last tick of budget. Its scheduling context drops to 0 and a refill is scheduled one period (20 ticks) out; the deadline stays where it is. alpha is requeued, but with no budget it is not eligible. Of beta and gamma, gamma's deadline is earlier, so gamma runs even though beta was queued first.

steps.title: tick: gamma spends a tick
steps.narrative: gamma spends one of its two ticks.

steps.title: tick: gamma's budget runs out
steps.narrative: gamma exhausts its budget too and waits for its refill. beta is the only eligible thread left, so it runs.

scenarios.title: Minting, copying, deleting and revoking
scenarios.summary: A supervisor derives capabilities from an endpoint master capability and then takes them back. Every derivation is recorded in the derivation tree, a derived capability can only lose rights, and revoking the master deletes everything derived from it.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The supervisor's CSpace holds, in slot 0, a capability to the CNode itself (with grant, which minting and copying need) and, in slot 1, the master capability to the log endpoint with read, write and grant. x0 = 0 names the CNode; the slots to operate on travel in x2 and x3.

steps.title: mint slot 1 → slot 4: write only, badge 7

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Require the grant right
Source CNode → destination CNode flow check
Mint a derived capability and link it under its source

steps.narrative: The rights mask 0b00010 asks for write alone, a subset of the master's rights, so the mint succeeds: slot 4 receives a write-only capability to the same endpoint, stamped with badge 7, and becomes the first child of slot 1 in the derivation tree.

steps.title: mint slot 4 → slot 5: read + write (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Require the grant right
Source CNode → destination CNode flow check
Mint: the requested rights are not a subset of the source's

steps.narrative: Slot 4 carries write only; this asks for read and write. A derived capability can never hold a right its source lacks, so the mint refuses with invalidCapability and slot 5 stays empty. The supervisor's own CNode capability passed every gate: the refusal is about the derivation, not about who asked.

steps.title: copy slot 4 → slot 6

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Require the grant right
Source CNode → destination CNode flow check
Copy the capability and link it under its source

steps.narrative: A copy keeps the source's rights and badge. Slot 6 becomes a child of slot 4, a grandchild of the master.

steps.title: mint slot 1 → slot 8: read only, badge 9

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Require the grant right
Source CNode → destination CNode flow check
Mint a derived capability and link it under its source

steps.narrative: A second child of the master: read only, badge 9. A new child goes to the front of its parent's child list, so slot 1's children now read 8, then 4.

steps.title: delete slot 4

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Require the write right
Delete the slot and splice its children into its parent

steps.narrative: Deleting a capability does not delete what was derived from it. Slot 4 is emptied and unlinked; its child, slot 6, is re-linked as a child of slot 4's parent, the master. The copy keeps its write right: revoking the master is still the way to take it back.

steps.title: revoke slot 1

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Require the write right
Delete the first child until none is left

steps.narrative: Revoke deletes everything derived from slot 1 and keeps slot 1 itself. It repeatedly deletes the source's first child: slot 6 (spliced in front by the delete), then slot 8. The master is left with no descendants.

scenarios.title: Carving and resetting untyped memory
scenarios.summary: All kernel memory starts as untyped regions. Retyping carves objects off the bottom of a region above a watermark that only rises; the region can be reset only once nothing refers to what was carved from it.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The memory manager holds a 16 KiB untyped region in slot 1 (with the retype right) and a capability to its own CNode in slot 0, where new capabilities land. Nothing has been carved yet: the watermark is at 0.

steps.title: retype a 4 KiB frame into slot 2

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Require the retype right
Carve the object above the watermark and install its capability

steps.narrative: x2 packs the object type (8, a frame) with its size bits (0: a frame is one page). The kernel carves 4 KiB at the watermark, moves the watermark to 4096, and installs a frame capability in slot 2 as a child of the untyped capability, so revoking the untyped reaches it.

steps.title: retype an 8 KiB untyped into slot 3

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Require the retype right
Carve the object above the watermark and install its capability

steps.narrative: An untyped can be split into smaller untypeds: type 5 with 13 size bits is 8 KiB. It is carved directly above the frame, so the two never overlap, and the watermark moves to 12288.

steps.title: retype another 8 KiB (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Require the retype right
Carve: 8192 bytes do not fit above the watermark

steps.narrative: 4 KiB remain above the watermark and 8 KiB were asked for. The carve refuses with untypedRegionExhausted; the watermark, the region's children and slot 4 are untouched.

steps.title: reset the untyped (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Require the retype right
Reset: carved objects are still referenced

steps.narrative: Resetting would hand the frame and the sub-untyped's memory out again while slots 2 and 3 still refer to them. The kernel refuses with revocationRequired: revoke first.

steps.title: revoke the untyped capability

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Require the write right
Delete the first child until none is left

steps.narrative: Every capability carved from the region is a child of the untyped capability, so revoking it deletes them: slot 3 first (the newest child is first), then slot 2.

steps.title: reset the untyped

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Require the retype right
Reset: scrub, flush and lower the watermark to 0

steps.narrative: Nothing refers to the carved objects any more. The region is scrubbed, stale translations are shot down, the children are forgotten and the watermark returns to 0.

scenarios.title: Mapping pages under W^X
scenarios.summary: A thread maps code and data into its address space. A page may be writable or executable, never both: a request for both is refused while decoding the permission word. Unmapping a page also removes its cached translation.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The app's address space (ASID 1) already maps its stack, and the translation is cached. Slot 1 holds the address-space capability; slots 2–4 hold frame capabilities: code (read), data and scratch (read and write). Permission words are bits r=1, w=2, x=4, user=8, cacheable=16.

steps.title: map code read + execute

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the address space)
Require the write right
Admit the frame, check the window and the walk, write the entry

steps.narrative: The permission word 0b11101 is read, execute, user and cacheable: W^X-compliant. The frame capability in slot 2 is looked up with read; a mapping that is not writable needs nothing more. The entry is written and the new translation is cached on the executing core.

steps.title: map data read + write

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the address space)
Require the write right
Admit the frame, check the window and the walk, write the entry

steps.narrative: Read and write without execute: compliant. A writable mapping needs a frame capability carrying write, which slot 3 has.

steps.title: map scratch read + write + execute (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the address space)
Require the write right
Decode the permission word: writable and executable

steps.narrative: The address-space capability passes the gate: the arm then decodes its arguments, and 0b11111 is both writable and executable. PagePermissions.ofNat? has no value for such a word, so the decode refuses with invalidSyscallArgument and no entry is written.

steps.title: unmap the stack

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the address space)
Require the write right
Clear the entry, shoot down the translation, invalidate the I-cache

steps.narrative: The entry is cleared and its cached translation is shot down on every core, so no core can still reach the frame through a stale TLB entry.

scenarios.title: Information flow and declassification
scenarios.summary: Security labels pair a confidentiality level with an integrity level. Information may flow to equal or higher confidentiality and to equal or lower integrity. A secret thread is refused when it writes down; a public thread may write up; and a write down happens only through declassification, which a policy must authorize and the kernel records.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: sec (secret: high confidentiality, untrusted) runs; pub (public: low, untrusted) waits to run; rcv (secret) waits on the secret endpoint. The declassification policy authorizes secret → public and nothing else.

steps.title: sec: send to the public endpoint (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1)
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send

steps.narrative: sec holds a perfectly good capability: the lookup and the rights check pass. But secret → public lowers confidentiality, so the flow gate refuses with flowDenied. Holding a capability is not enough; the labels must allow the flow as well.

steps.title: sec: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: sec yields and pub runs.

steps.title: pub: send to the secret endpoint

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1)
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send; a receiver waits, so deliver

steps.narrative: public → secret raises confidentiality and keeps integrity, so the flow is allowed. rcv is waiting on the endpoint and receives the word directly.

steps.title: pub: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: pub yields; sec is at the head of the bucket and runs.

steps.title: sec: declassify to the public endpoint

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the public endpoint)
Require the write right
Authorize the downgrade and record it

steps.narrative: Declassification is for exactly the flows the lattice denies: secret → public is denied, and the policy authorizes it, so the kernel admits the downgrade. Its only effect is an entry in the audit log naming who downgraded what, from which label to which; it writes no object and edits no policy.

scenarios.title: Two cores and thread affinity
scenarios.summary: Each core has its own run queue and current thread. Rebinding a queued thread to another core moves its queue entry; rebinding a thread that is running elsewhere is refused, because a running thread is in no queue to move.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: w0 runs on core 0 and w1 on core 1, with 1 tick of its slice left. w2 and w3 wait in core 1's queue. w0 holds TCB capabilities to w3 (slot 2) and w1 (slot 3).

steps.title: w0: bind w3 to core 0

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 2, w3's TCB)
Require the write right
Set the affinity and migrate the run-queue entry

steps.narrative: w3 is queued on core 1, not running, so its entry moves: out of core 1's queue and into core 0's. It does not preempt w0, whose priority is higher.

steps.title: w0: bind w1 to core 0 (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 3, w1's TCB)
Require the write right
Refuse: w1 is running on a core the new affinity excludes

steps.narrative: w1 is running on core 1. A running thread is in no run queue, so there is no entry to migrate, and leaving it running where its affinity forbids would break the scheduler's invariants. The kernel refuses with threadOnDifferentCore.

steps.title: core 1 tick: w1's slice runs out
steps.narrative: Core 1 ticks independently of core 0. w1's slice runs out and it is requeued, but it is still the highest priority thread on core 1, so it is picked again with a fresh slice.
